analyst_view.overall: Early view: two of the league's in-form sides. Bournemouth under Marco Rose have won eight straight in all competitions and Evanilson has scored in five league games in a row, while Brighton are second with 26 goals scored and only seven conceded. Bournemouth also play Celta Vigo in the Europa League on 26 November, which adds to an already busy run.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals. I lean slightly higher: Brighton average 2.6 goals a game and Bournemouth score freely in a high-intensity style, so both sides should find chances. Brighton's defence is the best in the league on goals conceded, which keeps me from going further.

corners.text: The site has 10.1 corners. I agree: Bournemouth's direct, wide attacks earn corners, and Brighton had almost 80% of the ball in the second half against Brentford, which also pins teams back. Both effects roughly balance the figure.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.8 cards. I lean lower: Brighton under Fabian Hurzeler keep the ball for long spells, which limits the stop-start fouling that brings cards, and neither club has a disciplinary problem in the news. A fast, open game between two good sides does not usually produce many bookings.

shots.text: The site has 26.1 shots. I lean higher because both teams want to attack: Bournemouth press and break quickly, and Brighton create a lot even without Kaoru Mitoma and Evan Ferguson. A busy game for both goalkeepers looks likely.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.1 shots on target. I lean higher: Brighton have scored 26 in 10 and Evanilson is in a hot streak, so the chances in this game should be good ones. Nine on target fits better.
